source_metadata.title: Mechanisms and Predisposing Conditions for Statin-Induced New-Onset Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Paradox Relative to Their Pleiotropic Metabolic Effects

batch_manifest.scope: objective, methods, statin pharmacology and shared context
insulin-secretion mechanisms and supporting study summaries
insulin-resistance mechanisms involving cholesterol, isoprenoids, GLUT4, lipid signaling, CoQ10/AMPK and PTEN
NLRP3/inflammation and other less-studied mechanisms including PXR, autophagy, acylcarnitines and adipocyte differentiation
human clinical evidence, statin-specific differences and risk modifiers

coverage.included: substantive article pages 1-13, including 2 tables and 3 figures
coverage.references: bibliography pages 14-18 excluded from atomization and used only for the reference task queue

duplicate_review.finding: No duplicate atom_id values; overlapping mechanistic claims were retained only when they represented distinct source assertions or evidence contexts.

consistency_findings: The review simultaneously characterizes rosuvastatin as among the more diabetogenic statins and later calls it the most suitable statin for preventing microvascular and macrovascular complications; this is a source-level interpretive tension, not repaired during extraction.
NLRP3 findings are explicitly contradictory across models; both activating and suppressive pathways were preserved as separate assertions.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema is oriented to primary literature and lacks a dedicated secondary-source or narrative-review assertion type. Underlying-study summaries are therefore tagged secondary_reported_result and anchored to this review; they must not be treated as primary-study extraction.
Clinical recommendations from a narrative review have no dedicated recommendation atom kind and are represented as author_conclusion with clinical_recommendation tags.
extraction_limitations: The review does not report reproducible search strings, study-selection flow, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or certainty grading.
Many cited-study summaries omit denominators, uncertainty intervals, or full comparator details; these were not invented.
Reference citations were not atomized; primary-study atoms require direct reading of the cited source.
